data.gender_notes: Mufarrij is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'faraja', which means 'to remove'. This name signifies a person who overcomes challenges and obstacles, making the way for others to follow. The name Mufarrij carries the meaning “One who removes obstacles” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mufarrij usually hope their child will grow to embody one who removes obstacles and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Mufarrij ibn Dirar Al-Kamili was an Arab poet from the Banu Kalb tribe who lived during the Umayyad period. He is known for his panegyrics in praise of the Umayyad caliphs Walid I and Hisham ibn Abdul Malik.

Mufarrij ibn al-Dahhak al-Qushairi was a renowned Islamic scholar and theologian from the city of Kus in Egypt, who lived during the Fatimid period. He is best known for his work 'Al-Risala al-Jami'ah fi Usul al-Fiqh', a comprehensive treatise on Islamic jurisprudence.
